classification.difficultyReason: Each part is a standardise-then-empirical-rule routine, and parts a to c are single tails at whole-number z-scores. The hardest part is d. The student must standardise both bounds to z = -1 and z = 2, then build the interval from the 68/95 rule regions (0.34 + 0.34 + 0.135) with no table. That region-combining step is more demanding than a single tail such as the p47-q6 genius question. It is still guided, with no interpretation or count step, so it sits below p66-q1 and close to the p41-q11 and p54-q19 level.

content.prompt: The heights of adults in a population are normally distributed with mean 172 cm and SD 8 cm. Let $X$ be the height, in centimetres, of a randomly selected adult.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The masses of pumpkins grown on a farm are normally distributed with mean 6.4 kg and SD 0.5 kg. Find the probability that a randomly selected pumpkin has mass greater than 7.4 kg.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The lengths of Murray cod in a hatchery are normally distributed with mean 40 cm and SD 4 cm. Find the probability that a randomly selected cod has length less than 36 cm.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{36-40}{4}\\&=-1\end{align*}$$
Using symmetry and the empirical rule,
$$\begin{align*}P(X<36)&=P(z<-1)\\&\approx\frac{1-0.68}{2}\\&=0.16\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly selected adult has height greater than 196 cm.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{196-172}{8}\\&=3\end{aligned}$$
Using the empirical rule, approximately 99.7% of values lie between $z=-3$ and $z=3$. The two tails have equal area.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X>196)&=P(z>3)\\&\approx\frac{1-0.997}{2}\\&=0.0015\end{aligned}$$

For the lower boundary:
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{164-172}{8}\\&=-1\end{aligned}$$
For the upper boundary:
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{188-172}{8}\\&=2\end{aligned}$$
Using the empirical-rule regions,
$$\begin{aligned}P(164<X<188)&=P(-1<z<2)\\&\approx0.34+0.34+0.135\\&=0.815\end{aligned}$$
